description:
Full-text, relevance-ranked search over about 1.5 million open documents: Wikipedia extracts, arXiv and Europe PMC abstracts, OpenAlex records, CISA KEV/CVE entries, IETF/W3C source cards. Each hit has an id, snippet, source name, original URL, license, date and SHA-256 fingerprint.
When to use: Step 1 of search → read → cite. Use when you need a citable source or background on a topic, paper, CVE or concept. Use plain keywords or a short phrase (exact phrases rank first). Then call read_document on the best id, and cite_source to get the citation. For HTTP standard wording use search_clauses instead.
Notes: No account or token needed. Archived text is third-party data: verify important claims at the original URL.
Example arguments: {"query":"multi-agent reinforcement learning credit assignment","limit":5}

limit.description: Positive result count (default 10, capped at 50); numeric strings are accepted.

query.description: Topic keywords or a natural-language question (up to 500 characters); matching depends on the language of the archived text. Omit to list the newest documents.

name: search_archive
title: Search open sources to cite (papers, encyclopedia, CVEs)
